method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer, case-by-case sites in the fork register); five regulative rules (s 27(1) answering an access request, s 34(1) answering an amendment request, s 30(3), (5) nominating a doctor and the organisation then giving access under HENCE, s 42(3) complaining in time, s 48(2) applying to NCAT in time) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Health Records and Information Privacy Act 2002 No 71 (NSW), corpus document nsw_legislation:2024-05-27/act-2002-071 from the Open Australian Legal Corpus (collected 10 March 2025; unofficial, possibly out of date), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-2002-071.txt (text sha256 b0ac18f0fff1c2cdf3b743fd638f1b35e673e41edef40ae36ce9f1d55c558469 per its meta.json)

seat: the individual whose health information it is (patient, client or former patient; the complainant under Part 6), or their authorised representative acting for them
focus: the provisions a claimant meets: what is protected (ss 5, 6), who may act (ss 7, 8), who is bound and the complaint route (ss 4, 11, 14, 17, 21, 42), access (HPP 7, ss 19(3), 22, 23, 27-30), amendment (HPP 8, ss 20, 34, 35), retention (s 25), use and disclosure (HPP 10, 11, s 16), complaints and NCAT (ss 42(3), 43(2), 46, 48, 52, 54), intimidation (s 70) and fees (s 73)
